review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its definitions (`fib`, `cFin`, `cInf`, `tensorAddHom`, `tensorRingHom`) against Mathlib. The only definition that competes with an existing Mathlib concept is the hand-built tensor-product universal map. I also noticed repeated theorems (`ringHom_ext_zp`/`ringHom_ext_R`, and `coeffMap_jqModC` stated twice). I excluded these under the rubric's carve-out for standalone theorem duplication. I did not confirm that the proposed replacement compiles. In particular, the `Algebra ℤp L` structure has to be chosen so that `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` can be applied, so the replacement is untested. The remaining uncertainty is whether the authors deliberately avoided introducing an algebra structure on the target.

findings.problem: The file rebuilds the universal property of the tensor product of commutative rings from scratch. `tensorAddHom` goes through `TensorProduct.liftAddHom`, and `tensorRingHom` proves `map_one'` and `map_mul'` by `TensorProduct.induction_on`. The result is a map `A ⊗ M → L` with `tmul x b ↦ F x * G b`. Mathlib already has this concept as `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` (for `f : A →ₐ[S] C` and `g : B →ₐ[R] C`) and `Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap`, both with `lift_tmul` / `productMap_apply_tmul`. The custom version's only difference is that it takes plain ring homs and gets compatibility on ℤp from `ringHom_ext_zp`. That compatibility is exactly the fact that `F.comp (algebraMap ℤp A) = G.comp (algebraMap ℤp M)`. It is equivalent to putting an `Algebra ℤp L` structure on the target (for example `(F.comp (algebraMap ℤp A)).toAlgebra`) and viewing F and G as algebra homs. The file already uses `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` in `InfOffC1Main.sectionFibre_eq`, so it has two parallel tensor-lift APIs. The custom one has only the `_tmul` lemma and no `comp_includeLeft` / `comp_includeRight` or uniqueness lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `tensorAddHom` and `tensorRingHom`. At the two uses (`InfOffC1Alg.false_of_one_tmul_eq_pow` and the `Nontrivial (κ ⊗[R p] O0)` instance in `InfOffC1Main.dict`), put a ℤp-algebra structure on the target via `RingHom.toAlgebra` of the composite from ℤp. Then apply `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` (or `productMap`) to F and G, using `Commute.all _ _`, and read off `RingHom.domain_nontrivial` / the tmul value with `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift_tmul`. If the plain ring-hom orientation is wanted, keep only a thin named wrapper around `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` and drop the manual `induction_on` multiplicativity proof.
findings.benefit: It removes about 40 lines of bespoke definition and proof. It also gives the tensor lift the simp lemmas and compatibility with `includeLeft`/`includeRight`/`map` that Mathlib already provides. Readers no longer have to compare two lift constructions in the same file, and the result composes with the rest of Mathlib's `Algebra.TensorProduct` API.

evidence.excerpt: def lift (f : A →ₐ[S] C) (g : B →ₐ[R] C) (hfg : ∀ x y, Commute (f x) (g y)) : (A ⊗[R] B) →ₐ[S] C :=
theorem productMap_apply_tmul (a : A) (b : B) : productMap f g (a ⊗ₜ b) = f a * g b := rfl
